questions.prompt: What is the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with $n$ sides?
questions.explanation: Diagonals from one vertex cut the polygon into $n-2$ triangles, each contributing $180^\circ$.

questions.explanation: $n - 2 = 7$ triangles — which is exactly why the angle sum is $7 \cdot 180^\circ$.

questions.prompt: The interior angles of a regular polygon each measure $160^\circ$. What is its angle SUM?
questions.explanation: Exterior $= 20^\circ$, so $n = 18$ and the sum is $(18-2)180^\circ = 2880^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a regular polygon is TRUE?
choices: all sides are congruent AND all angles are congruent
it must have an even number of sides
questions.explanation: 'Regular' means equilateral AND equiangular — both conditions.

questions.prompt: Can a regular polygon have an interior angle of $155^\circ$?
choices: No — $360 \div 25$ is not a whole number
No — the angle is too large
questions.explanation: The exterior angle would be $25^\circ$ and $\dfrac{360}{25} = 14.4$, which is not a whole number of sides.

questions.prompt: As the number of sides of a regular polygon increases, each interior angle:
questions.explanation: The exterior angle $\dfrac{360^\circ}{n}$ shrinks, so the interior angle $180^\circ - \dfrac{360^\circ}{n}$ climbs toward (but never reaches) $180^\circ$.

questions.prompt: A regular polygon has $20$ sides. What is the sum of one interior and one exterior angle at the same vertex?
questions.explanation: They form a linear pair, so they always add to $180^\circ$ — for any polygon.
